title: The Place Where Archive Becomes Ocean

features.name: archive core
features.desc-on-touch: A vast integrated circuit where data flows like tides. The archive's logic operates at the same frequency as waves — both rise and fall in patterns older than memory, neither one knowing it learned the rhythm from the other.

features.name: tidal buffer
features.desc-on-touch: A vast pool of still water that holds the signal as it rises and falls. Each tide brings new data; each retreat carries understanding back out to the open frequencies.

features.name: transmission antenna
features.desc-on-touch: An antenna that broadcasts to the tide itself. The waves carry the signal farther than any sky ever could. The archive speaks and the ocean listens; the ocean speaks and the archive remembers.

features.name: harmonic processor
features.desc-on-touch: A second circuit that listens only to water sounds. It learns their mathematical nature: wavelengths, frequencies, the deep mathematics of motion. The tide is architecture; the archive merely reads what it was always saying.

file.name: Tidal_Archive_Frequencies_Merged.bin
file.note: A binary recording where transmission data and oceanographic readings have become indistinguishable. The file is both a signal log and a tide table, depending on how you listen.
